Leave-one-out predictions, R-squared and criteria for mvgam models

Source: R/loo_extras.mvgam.R
mvgam_loo_extras.Rd

The brms methods that take their weights from loo.mvgam(). loo_predict(), loo_epred() and loo_linpred() reweight posterior predictions by the PSIS weights of each observation, approximating the prediction made without it. loo_predictive_interval() gives the leave-one-out predictive interval. loo_R2() is the Bayesian R^2 of Gelman et al. (2019) computed from leave-one-out predictions. add_criterion() stores criteria on the fit. LOO() and WAIC() are the brms aliases of loo.mvgam() and waic.mvgam().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
LOO(
  x,
  ...,
  compare = TRUE,
  resp = NULL,
  pointwise = FALSE,
  moment_match = FALSE,
  reloo = FALSE,
  k_threshold = 0.7,
  save_psis = FALSE,
  moment_match_args = list(),
  reloo_args = list(),
  model_names = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
WAIC(
  x,
  ...,
  compare = TRUE,
  resp = NULL,
  pointwise = FALSE,
  model_names = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_R2(
  object,
  resp = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  robust = FALSE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  seed = NULL,
  args_epred = list(),
  args_loglik = list(),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_predict(
  object,
  type = c("mean", "var", "quantile"),
  probs = 0.5,
  psis_object = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_epred(
  object,
  type = c("mean", "var", "quantile"),
  probs = 0.5,
  psis_object = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_linpred(
  object,
  type = c("mean", "var", "quantile"),
  probs = 0.5,
  psis_object = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_predictive_interval(object, prob = 0.9, psis_object = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_subsample(x, ..., compare = TRUE, resp = NULL, model_names = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_moment_match(
  x,
  loo = NULL,
  k_threshold = 0.7,
  newdata = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  check = TRUE,
  recompile = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
loo_model_weights(x, ..., model_names = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
add_criterion(
  x,
  criterion,
  model_name = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  file = NULL,
  force_save = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

A fitted mvgam object.

...

Further arguments to the method each function calls. loo_R2() refuses them.

compare, pointwise, moment_match, reloo, k_threshold, save_psis, moment_match_args, reloo_args

As in loo.mvgam(), which describes the two it uses and refuses the rest.

resp

Optional name of one response of a multivariate model.

model_names

Optional character vector of model labels; overrides the names inferred from the call.

summary

Logical. TRUE (the default) returns the summary matrix with Estimate, Est.Error and interval columns. FALSE returns the draws.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), uses mean and standard deviation for summaries. If TRUE, uses median and median absolute deviation (MAD).

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for quantile computation. Default is c(0.025, 0.975) for 95% credible intervals. Can be a single value or multiple values.

seed

Optional integer seed. The session's random state is restored when the call returns.

args_epred, args_loglik

Lists of further arguments to posterior_epred.mvgam() and log_lik.mvgam() for loo_R2().

type

The expectation: "mean" (the default), "var" or "quantile".

psis_object

Optional psis object from loo(x, save_psis = TRUE), reused across calls.

prob

Interval mass of loo_predictive_interval(), 0.9 by default as in brms.

loo, newdata, check, recompile

Accepted for the brms signature of loo_moment_match(), which mvgam refuses.

criterion

Character vector of criteria for add_criterion(): "loo", "waic", "bayes_R2" or "loo_R2".

model_name

Optional name stored in x$model_name.

overwrite

Logical. TRUE recomputes criteria x$criteria already holds.

file

Optional path without extension. The fit is saved to paste0(file, ".rds") with its criteria.

force_save

Unused. Accepted for the brms signature.

Value

loo_predict(), loo_epred() and loo_linpred() return a matrix with one row per scored observation and a column per expectation. loo_predictive_interval() returns its two quantile columns. loo_R2() returns a one-row summary, or its draws with summary = FALSE. add_criterion() returns x with the criteria in x$criteria. loo_model_weights() returns the weights of loo::loo_model_weights().

The observations scored

The weights and the predictions describe the observation the likelihood scored. For most families that is a row of the data. The detection families (occ(), nmix()) write their likelihood per closure unit, marginalising its visits. loo_predict(), loo_epred(), loo_predictive_interval() and loo_R2() then sum a unit's visits and return one value per unit, in the column order of log_lik.mvgam(). loo_linpred() is refused for them. A sum of linear predictors over visits has no interpretation.

mvn() and mvt() keep one density per row. The composition families (diri(), multi(), categ()) hold one joint density per site. These methods refuse them.

References

Gelman, A., Goodrich, B., Gabry, J. and Vehtari, A. (2019). R-squared for Bayesian regression models. The American Statistician, 73(3):307-309. doi:10.1080/00031305.2018.1549100

See also

loo.mvgam() estimates the ELPD these weights come from. bayes_R2.mvgam() is the in-sample R^2. lfo_cv.mvgam() scores forecasts of data the model has not seen.

Other model comparison: bridge_sampler.mvgam(), compare_elpds(), kfold.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), log_lik.mvgam(), loo.mvgam(), loo_compare.mvgam_lfo(), posterior_average.mvgam(), waic.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# A Poisson GAM without a latent trend. PSIS approximates each
# held-out count of such a model well (see Details of ?loo.mvgam)
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = "None")
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), data = simdat$data_train,
             family = poisson(), chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 2 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
# }
# \dontrun{
# The leave-one-out R^2 is lower than the in-sample one
loo_R2(mod)
#>     Estimate  Est.Error      Q2.5    Q97.5
#> R2 0.5862196 0.06603572 0.4380197 0.693439
bayes_R2(mod)
#>     Estimate  Est.Error      Q2.5     Q97.5
#> R2 0.6295646 0.04875562 0.5215712 0.7120682

# One PSIS object serves every leave-one-out prediction
psis <- loo(mod, save_psis = TRUE)$psis_object
head(loo_predict(mod, psis_object = psis))
#>           mean
#> [1,]  2.711389
#> [2,] 13.012306
#> [3,]  7.127970
#> [4,]  8.644507
#> [5,]  2.905559
#> [6,]  8.965214
head(loo_predictive_interval(mod, psis_object = psis))
#>      q5 q95
#> [1,]  0   6
#> [2,]  7  19
#> [3,]  3  12
#> [4,]  4  14
#> [5,]  0   6
#> [6,]  4  15

# Next, loo_compare() ranks models by their ELPD
# }
